questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to a place en the UK or Ireland to improve my English and get to know that culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience. I really enjoyed experiencing the place and getting to know people from all over the world. It was also really tiring and overwhelming at times, cause you wanted to make the most of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I think. It all went pretty smoothly. But there was a lot of information to keep track of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of mails mainly and a meeting with my student counselor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. I went on spareroom and luckily a girl wrote me and asked if I wanted to join a flat search. From what I have heard it can be quite difficult to find people on there though since people mainly want someone who can stay for more than a semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive and maybe require more work to get to know people from uni, since you don't meet them at a student accommodation. For me it was a really good experience since I got to live with three other lovely girls.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know much about the student housings available, but from what I have heard it is quite expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I made a priority list of courses I wanted and was lucky enough to get my top three picks. I did end up switching one of the courses for another. It was easy enough but I had to make sure my courses didn't clash in my schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student counselors. They were very helpful in making changes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got the courses I wanted. But it was a bit of work to figure out which courses I was able to apply for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start looking at the courses well in advance but remember you can switch when you get there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked two of the three courses I took. Especially the one I took different from my normal degree that was about Scotland and its oral traditions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was alright for me. Some of it was challenging but also not too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot less tutorials than I am used to. So the days at school was shorter and I had to do more work outside of school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology. Structures and Functions of Proteins. Scotland and Orality.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Scotland and Orality. It was different from what im used to. But felt very relevant to learn something about scottish culture while you're there.

questions.answer: I think just exploring the city and experiencing stuff costs money which was a bit unexpected.

questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many opportunities. So many sports and almost anything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe the folk dancing or folk music. I went to some of the events which were very funny.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands on walks if the weather is nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy I think. It is not too different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly that the cars drive on the other side of the road. Otherwise I didn't find anything too challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The humor I think.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
People are usually a bit younger than danish students, since they being uni at 18. But I don't think it matters too much in the end. 
It's a really nice and walkable city to live in. So it's really a nice place to explore. 
You need to set more time off to do coursework, since that sometimes counts in your final grade.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult at first starting up. But shortly after it will be alright.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet a lot of people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think in the beginning it was really a challenge to get to know a new place, a new uni and new people. But after getting used to the place it really became a great experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
